body:
**Market regime filter: follow-through day (FTD) and distribution days (IBD)**
- FTD: on Day 4 or later of a rally attempt (Day 1 = first up close after a new low), a major index (Nasdaq or S&P 500) gains a minimum percentage on volume higher than the prior session; strongest FTDs come on days 4-7. Threshold has changed over time: ~1% in the original rule, ~1.7% in IBD's 2000s rule, ~1.25% in recent descriptions (not confirmed against an IBD primary document). The FTD fails if the index undercuts the rally-attempt low. — [LuxAlgo: Follow-through Day](https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/follow-through-day/) [F]
- Distribution day: index closes down at least 0.2% on volume higher than the prior session; each counts for 25 sessions, and drops off early if the index rallies 5% above that day's close. Clusters of ~5-6 distribution days within 25 sessions are IBD's warning that the uptrend is "under pressure." — [LuxAlgo: Distribution Days](https://www.luxalgo.com/library/concept/distribution-days/) [F] (third-party; not IBD primary)

- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:SBICARD:q3fy27-gnpa-at-or-below-1-90`
- **Method:** sector cycle/lead indicator · **P(ours)** 0.55 · **P(base)** 0.65 · resolve by 2027-02-15
- **Evidence:** Q2 FY27 call (29-Oct-2026): GNPA 1.90% (−14 bps QoQ, −95 bps YoY), NNPA 0.77%, gross credit cost 5.6% (−98 bps QoQ); management overlay raised by ₹30 cr to ₹100 cr citing 'prolonged conflict in West Asia… higher energy prices, inflation and interest rates may impact household cash flows'; guide 'gross credit costs to stay around 6% for the current financial year' and 'we don't expect the credit costs to moderate much beyond' 5.5–6%; cost of funds 6.8% (+18 bps QoQ) and 'expected to increase over the next few quarters'; receivables ₹58,376 cr, festive spends to lift receivables in Q3. Screener GNPA: Jun-24 3.06%, Sep-24 3.27%, Dec-24 3.24%, Mar-25 3.08%, Jun-25 3.07%, Sep-25 2.85%, Dec-25 2.86%, Mar-26 2.41%, Jun-26 2.04%, Sep-26 1.90%.
- **Why our number differs from base:** Lead indicator: RBI has hiked (repo 5.5%, more expected), fuel inflation is squeezing households, and management itself built an overlay and called the credit-cost bottom. Unsecured card delinquencies respond to rate/inflation shocks with a 1–3 quarter lag. Festive receivable growth (bigger denominator) helps the ratio, so we stay just above even, but below the trend-following base.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Trend persistence: GNPA has fallen in each of the last four quarters; a naive forecaster gives ~65% to another non-rise.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if SBI Cards and Payment Services' reported gross NPA ratio (% of gross advances/receivables) for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 is ≤1.90% (two decimals as reported).
- **Resolution source:** SBI Cards Q3 FY27 results / investor presentation (NSE) / screener.in quarterly table
- **Sources used:** https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/SBICPSL_29102026165052_SEfilingtranscriptoct2026.pdf; https://www.screener.in/company/SBICARD/
- **Confidence of evidence:** verified

body:
- **Insider (PIT) data is stale at the source.** NSE's PIT feed has no records dated after
  30-Apr-2026, both the all-market query and per-symbol queries (checked 21-Nov-2026), and BSE's
  insider endpoint returned nothing. So `insider_buy`, `insider_sell` and the PIT half of
  `insider_cluster` cannot fire until NSE resumes; `collect.py` logs a warning every day while it is
  stale. Promoter open-market trades still arrive through SAST Reg 29 (`sast_promoter_open_market`,
  and clusters built from SAST rows), but SAST has no rupee value, covers promoters only (not
  directors or KMP), and only applies to trades above the SAST reporting thresholds. The code keeps
  calling PIT (all-market, then per-symbol for up to 25 companies a day) so it recovers by itself.
- About 80 of about 1,500 companies in the pledge snapshot are not matched to an NSE symbol (mostly
  BSE-only or delisted names). They are logged and skipped.
- Announcement rules are keyword rules on the exchange's one-line text. They catch most events,
  with some false positives (read the filing) and misses where the detail is only inside the PDF.
- Bulk/block deal percentages need a share count: from the pledge snapshot, otherwise from the
  latest shareholding-pattern XBRL (cached for 100 days).
- NSE moved its host to `www.nseindia.in` in 2026 and changes endpoints without notice. If a
  selftest line fails, the endpoint has probably changed; the raw files show what came back.

| Type | Meaning | Calls | Automation |
|---|---|---|---|
| a | reported number vs threshold (revenue, margin, op profit, growth, EPS, NII, pledge %, NIM, GNPA, AUM, VNB, order inflow…) | 48 | 28 structured (22 India via NSE XBRL + screener, incl. the INDOTECH pledge; 6 US via SEC XBRL), 20 assisted (company-defined KPIs in press releases/decks/8-K exhibits) |
| b | price return vs Nifty 50 / SPY (Yahoo v8 closes) | 7 | 7 structured |
| c | corporate event or guidance (8-K 1.03 bankruptcy, dividend raise, buyback, regulatory order, deal closing, commissioning, ICFR remediation, initial guidance) | 18 | 2 structured (OPTU 8-K 1.03, CAT dividend), 16 assisted |
| d | human judgment (basis "as the company counts it", "most popular plan") | 4 | AUBANK, TATAPOWER, NTPC, BHARTIARTL |

`structured` = the resolver may decide. `assisted` = the resolver finds the documents, pulls snippets and the
first number that matches, and *proposes* an outcome; a human confirms. `human` = judgment queue (it still
gathers documents). The heuristic classifier agrees with the curated type on 75 of the 77 calls. The two
differences are deliberate: TRANSRAILL is kept as type a, and NTPC is kept as type d.

body:
- SQLite runs in WAL mode with `synchronous=NORMAL`, an 8 MB page cache and one commit per
  dataset per day, so each evening is a handful of sequential writes. The WAL is checkpointed at
  the end of `collect.py`.
- Raw files are gzipped JSON, roughly 0.3 to 0.5 MB per trading day.
- The heaviest step, the all-company pledge snapshot, holds one JSON response of about 1,500 rows in
  memory. Peak memory of a full run is measured below.
- A full evening run makes roughly 100 to 150 HTTP requests spaced at least 1.5 s apart, so it takes
  a few minutes. 403/429/5xx get exponential back-off (5, 10, 20 s), then the step is logged as
  failed and the run moves on.
- To look at the data: `sqlite3 ~/fein-data/fein.sqlite "select * from alerts order by first_seen desc limit 20"`.

| Lender test | screener labels Banks / NBFC / Housing Finance / Microfinance / Financial Institution. Unlabeled (mostly merged/delisted) pages classified by name; 39 ambiguous names ("capital", "invest") not counted (none was in band). Holding companies of a single lender and NBFC-CICs reviewed by hand and counted: Equitas Holdings, IDFC Ltd, Reliance Capital. Diversified holdcos (Edelweiss, JM Financial), brokers, AMCs, insurers excluded |
| Start dates T | 30-Sep-2016, 30-Sep-2018; FY0 annual column in (T−18m, T−6m]; a weekly price within 31 days before T |
| Size | screener market-cap-to-sales × TTM sales at the last price ≤ T, **₹1,000–20,000 cr**; 2 overrides where the ratio is missing in an IPO month (RBL Aug-2016 ₹11,100 cr, CreditAccess Aug-2018 ₹5,300 cr; shares × screener price, single-source) |
| ≥3x / ≤0.5x | R5 = price at T+5 ÷ price at T (price only). No R5 + failure → ≤0.5x |
| Blow-up | close ≤0.2× the T close at any point within 5 yrs, liquidation, compulsory delisting, **equity write-off** (LVB Nov-2020). Also reported: **permanent blow-up** = blow-up AND (R5 ≤0.5x or no R5) |
| Mergers | Not dropped: the holder's path is chained into the acquirer at the target's last traded price (R = target_last/target_T × acquirer(t)/acquirer(link)), so split adjustments in the acquirer series do not matter. 24 rows chained (8 PSU-bank amalgamations, 3 SBI associates, GRUH, Capital First is not in band, Bharat Financial, Shriram City, Equitas Holdings) |
| Median multiple | median R5 with failed-no-R5 = 0 |
| CI | 2,000 bootstrap draws, companies resampled (a company in both snapshots is one cluster), seed 20261125 |

Input: `research_notes/News/first_run_2026-11-25.md` (headlines only, single source). This note checks each material flag that bears on an
open paper call for UTTAMSUGAR, UTKARSHBNK, US-NVDA, US-NEE, US-UNH, INDRAMEDCO, SUNFLAG, POLYCAB, ICICIBANK, TVSMOTOR and MARICO.
Roadmap: stage 2 (hard filters: governance/legal), stage 4 (deep-dive facts), stage 7 (scorekeeping context). It unlocks the L45
administered-price calendar (`research_notes/Deep dives/UTTAMSUGAR_price_calendar.md`) and dated event records for later Brier reviews.

**Rules used.** "Confirmed" means a primary document (exchange filing, SEC 8-K, RBI release), or two independent reputable outlets.
"Partly" means the core event is real but the headline's framing or a detail is not supported. "Unconfirmed" means we could not find
a primary document or a second outlet. "False/stale" means the primary record contradicts the headline or shows it is out of date.
**No paper call, probability or date was changed.** The "bears on" column gives a direction only.
Research, not SEBI-registered advice.
